Press,
"s" to save a screenshot in 4k
"p" to switch to black and white
"space" to pause
"left arrow" to step back
"right arrow" to step forward

Original artwork by William Watkins · Lyon, 2022

Mixed Signals is a series of 128 generative animated loops. Each animation is constructed with a grid of curves that creates illusions of waveforms marching across the screen or shapes bubbling in and out of existence. Some rare mints are possible, since features are available in the following categories:

extremely low, very low, low, medium, high, very high, extremely high

where medium is the most common, low and high are rarer, very low and very high are even rarer, etc.

Interactions:
Ctrl+S / Cmd+S: Save a 2048 x 2048 screen capture
Ctrl+Shift+S / Cmd+Shift+S (Press, don't hold): Export image sequence of 3 second loop 
Space bar: Pause/Unpause the animation

Original artwork by Stephen Jue · Made with canvas-sketch · 2022

5536.d:
Generates realistic looking trees from a chaotic fractal 
Based on my dweet here - https://www.dwitter.net/d/24167


Unlike IFS fractals which are designed to draw a certain shape, this particular fractal happens to generate these forms serendipitiously - which is quite a wonder.

The fractal itself needs only a few lines of code to generate.


Random colored skies and clouds are drawn, as well as moon an stars for the night-mode variations.
The image is rendered incrementally and takes about 10 seconds to generate.  


Features available:

Time: Day/Night/Dusk
Sky: Clear/Cloudy/Overcast
Season: Spring/Summer/Fall
Tree shape: Bent/Straight/Scrubby 
Tree spread: large/small

It is a seek words consisting of 4 squares by 4 squares.

Hot Hamon is a mesmerizing loop of rotating dynamic lines. 
Enjoy the slow dance of lines, a swirling abstract shape, changing Moire patterns or follow a single line like a slow ceiling fan. 

This code began as a simple animation of two invisible rotating ellipses and visible lines connecting the closest endpoints of the two ellipses. I quickly realized by heavily distorting the ellipse shapes, the lines between them made abstract shapes and mesmerizing Moire patterns. So I kept distorting and tweaking the code till it got to here. 

Attributes:
6 math functions for x an y
6 colors
5 sizes
3 shape styles
3 line sets
3 line types
2 background styles
2 spin directions - counter clockwise is rare


About me:
Hey I’m Will, an architect and artist from Atlanta. After becoming an architect I began making trippy art at night as a way to learn code. Now I’m here a few years later with my first NFT, still can only code art, but that's fine by me.

Evolution is change in the heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations. These characteristics are the expressions of genes that are passed on from parent to offspring during reproduction. Different characteristics tend to exist within any given population as a result of mutation, genetic recombination and other sources of genetic variation. Evolution occurs when evolutionary processes such as natural selection and genetic drift act on this variation, resulting in certain characteristics becoming more common or rare within a population. The circumstances that determine whether a characteristic should be common or rare within a population constantly change, resulting in the change in heritable characteristics arising over successive generations. 

Part of the f series.

Four colors have the capacity to make up the entire spectrum of printed work. Here on the digital screen, their purpose is destroyed. Cyan, magenta, yellow, and black are enlarged, torn apart, and blended back together to form something new. 

Build up each color in turn using the left and right arrows. 
Bring all colors back with the return key.
Separate each color from its neighbor with the up arrow.
Align each color accurately with the down arrow.
Reset the initial state of each color with the delete key.
Press the space bar to show and hide the derived image.

In Greek mythology Polyphemus was a one-eyed giant, a Cyclops, the son of Poseidon and Thoosa. In the Odyssey, he battles Odysseus and is blinded by the hero.

"Then from out the cave the mighty Polyphemus answered them: 'My friends, it is Noman that is slaying me by guile and not by force.' "
    ~ Homer's Odyssey, Book 9

Yes, Polyphemus was a monster - a man eating, one-eyed giant - but was there more to his story? Odysseus and his men did trespass and eat his food. They went on their adventure looking for "monsters" to kill, and they found them.  But "monster"?  If you mess with a snake and it bites you, you don't blame the snake do you? 

Maybe there's more to these characters. Like us, maybe they have (or had) lives and just want to be left alone. 


--- 

Three variations:

- No inner frame
- Inner frame
- Inner frame with artist's signature (rare)

Originally based on Alberto Burri's 1973- 1976 Screen Prints, then further iterated upon: Fleur des Sinus is meant to play with abstraction by designing larger than the canvas. Creating something that's clearly defined and pushing in just enough to find new compositions in section and intersection.

There are two possible modes, changing the shape of the flowers.
26 palettes are available, each composed of 4 colors: 104 colors in total.
A palette is picked for each edge flower, the center flower expresses itself with no inhibitions.
The Flowers are made up of between 4-10 petals.
The background pattern is 1-6 petal minimal dot flower patterns.

Press 's' to save the image in Live View.

Assigning different rules to these particles creates very interesting patterns. In this piece they are taught to move in ever increasing circles creating a snail pattern. 

Colors, stroke width, straight/curved lines are determined by the hash. In some iterations particles will gravitate to each other, creating a more chaotic pattern.

S - Save 2000x2000 image
Space - Pause/Unpause animation
Up/Down-Arrows - Increase/Decrease speed

5708.d:
The AI sees the sunset 20 times in a day. One loves the sunset, when one is so sad.

Never in history have we been so dependent on machines. I also think art should keep up with AI as it evolves. So when I ask an AI to draw up abstract sunsets for 20 times, what will it see? And can I collaborate with it to make it more organic?

Technical Notes: OpenAI's GLIDE model, with prompt “an abstract painting of a sunset” that turned the text into images for 20 time, each took about 20 minutes on a macbook pro. Then based on the output, I used the Floyd-Steinberg Dithering technique to calculate the values to be painted. Finally I tuned the strokes and landed on using giant circles (the edges of these circles to be exact) to paint for a more organic feel.

5722.d:
Technical Drawing classes I took many years ago often focused on using isometric projections to create detailed diagrams of complex objects. I remember being fascinated by how a few simple lines created the illusion of three dimensions and gave expression to the maths behind the geometry. 

This piece reminds me of those plans and diagrams I used to draw. It plays with perception, flipping between 2D and 3D and invites you to believe that perhaps they are remnants of some grand idea. 

—

Generative properties include colour selection, cube arrangement and cube configuration. 

Shortcut keys:
W - toggle wide-screen 16:9 vs square 1:1 format 
S - save as an image

 Made with code and love by AutoEclectus in Australia.

 AutoEclectus is a visual artist specialising in code-based generative works.

5736.d:
This is the second generative work from "Faceless". Like the first one, it is a series of generative collages, only this time I managed to keep the work defined for each hash.

The spread of pictures are derived and painted over from a screenshot from “Les Yeux sans visage” (Eyes Without a Face ); a black and white French film from 1960, directed by Georges Franju. It is adapted by Pierre Boileau and Thomas Narcejac from the novel by Jean Redon.

In the film; Dr. Génessier causes an accident which leaves his daughter Christiane disfigured and he goes to extreme lengths to give her a new face. During the process Christiane (portrayed by Edith Scob) wears the mask used here.

“My face frightens me. My mask frightens me even more.”
5736.c: "Faceless" is a multi-disciplanary project where I plan to combine these generate works with my interest in cinema. Along with the collages here, I am minting photos and videos over at HEN as well.

5744.d:
Biological and inorganic matter often grow from a tiny seed. After leaving the seed, the trunk unfurls into an array of possibilities. After some time has passed, the seed is reborn.

Some seeds can take longer to grow than others. All seeds begin in the middle.

A couple resolutions: 256, 512, 1024, 2048 (larger is rarer)
All other parameters change the behavior, colorization, and animation of each piece.
This is a larger edition, since the parameter space is very wide.

Each piece is lightly interactive. During growth, more seeds can be added by clicking and drawing into untraversed territory.

When viewing the piece live, you can press the 's' key to take a capture. Captures may be scaled to any desired resolution using 'nearest-neighbor' scaling.

Made with p5.js, p5Fbo.js, and glsl

5746.d:
This art aims to remember the traces of crayons scratching blackboards and even walls, if you prefer. In a child's hands, a crayon represents freedom to draw whatever he wants, even if it's an indefinite scribble. And with these scribbles, I bring to this code the straight, horizontal and vertical lines, which intersect, always mixing two palettes, thus obtaining a perception of incredible depth and texture.

Carefully chosen color palettes.

FEATURES:
> Crayons Amount 🖍: 300 to 1100.
> Vertical Crayons Palette 🎨: Education levels.
> Horizontal Crayons Palette 🎨: Education levels.
> Classroom Blackboard Color ⬛️: Somethings to study.
> Color Effect¹: Normal ★, Negative Mode ★★ or GrayScale Mode ★★★.

RARITY BONUS: 
> (★) = rarity level: ★ = 85%, ★★ = 15%, ★★★ = 5%.
> If you got ★★ or ★★★, you will discover

INTERACTIVE MODS, PRESS ANYTIME: 
> "P" to pause/play.
> "S" to save a .png of your canvas (in Open Live).
> "N" to switch the Negative, if you got one.
> "G" to switch the GrayScale, if you got one.
